answer: Practically, the chain should stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because island only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, mesa is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
